output.summary: A perennial herb native to northern North America from Alaska to New York and south to Arizona and New Mexico, and also known from parts of South America. Its appearance varies greatly among varieties, with deeply divided hairy leaves and usually white petal-like sepals. It is poisonous and contains high levels of ranunculin in its above-ground parts and roots.
output.edibilityNote: Poisonous; its above-ground parts and roots contain high levels of ranunculin.
